mainTopic: With one cup of wine: why קידוש is done right away but הבדלה can wait, and the eight lessons drawn from the הבדלה ברייתא
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא: a person with only one cup of wine uses it for קידוש at night, because קידוש היום comes before כבוד יום. רבינא asks why he doesn't wait until the next day and use the one cup for two מצוות at once. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers חביבה מצוה בשעתה: a מצוה is most precious when done at its proper time. רבינא challenges this from a ברייתא about הבדלה. There, a person with one cup saves it until after the meal. רב נחמן בר יצחק humbly says he is only passing on the accepted ruling. He then explains that bringing שבת in and taking it out are different. We bring שבת in early to show love for it, and take it out late so it won't seem like a burden. The גמרא then says the הבדלה ברייתא teaches eight lessons, and lists six of them here. הבדלה in the תפלה still needs a cup, ברכת המזון needs a cup, and the cup needs a minimum amount. The one who blesses must drink, drinking makes the cup פגום, and eating first does not cancel הבדלה. The list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: With one cup, קידוש at night comes first
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא: with only one cup, it goes to קידוש היום, because קידוש comes before honoring the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: [He uses the one cup for] the קידוש of the day, because קידוש of the day comes before the honor of the day (and the honor of the night).
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last words of a ברייתא that the גמרא started quoting on the previous amud. It says that a person with only one cup of wine should use it for קידוש on Friday night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ranks two uses of wine. Saying קידוש to bring in שבת outranks drinking wine to honor the שבת meal. Everything that follows next is built on this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctifying the day; the קידוש said to bring in שבת
Honoring the day, here by having wine at the daytime meal
Comes first; takes priority

phrases.english: [He uses it for] the sanctification of the day,
phrases.notes: The end of a ברייתא quoted earlier about someone with only one cup.

phrases.english: because the sanctification of the day comes first
before the honor of the day (and the honor of the night).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקִּידּוּשׁ הַיּוֹם קוֹדֵם לִכְבוֹד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא whose quotation began on the previous amud (105a).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With only one cup, use it for קידוש at night, because קידוש היום outranks כבוד יום.

steps.title: Why not wait and use the cup for two things?
steps.stepSummary: If one can make קידוש during the day, why not save the cup for tomorrow and do two מצוות with it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if so, let him leave the cup until tomorrow and do two things with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner (רבינא, according to the Sefaria translation) challenges the ruling. He asks why the person doesn't save the cup for the next day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who missed קידוש at night can still make it during the day. So waiting until morning would let one cup cover both קידוש and כבוד יום. Using the cup at night seems wasteful by comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so (if what you said is true)
Let him leave it
Two things

phrases.english: And if it is so —
phrases.notes: That is, if קידוש can be made during the day.

phrases.english: let him leave it until tomorrow,
and do two things with it!
phrases.notes: Daytime קידוש and כבוד יום with the same cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling to use the single cup for קידוש at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Waiting until day lets one cup cover two מצוות instead of one, so that should be preferred.

steps.title: A מצוה is most precious at its proper time
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers: חביבה מצוה בשעתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A מצוה is beloved at its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains why we don't wait. A מצוה done at its correct time is especially precious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing two things with one cup does not beat doing קידוש at its real time, Friday night. Daytime קידוש is only a backup. You shouldn't plan to use the backup.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה is beloved (most precious) at its proper time

phrases.english: He said to him: A מצוה is beloved at its proper time.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a value principle that outweighs efficiency.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Using one cup for two מצוות is best, so you should wait until the day.
steps.terutzMaskana: Doing the מצוה at its proper time is more important, so make קידוש at night.

steps.title: But with הבדלה we do wait!
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that someone with one cup on מוצאי שבת holds it until after the meal for הבדלה. So we don't apply חביבה מצוה בשעתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really say a מצוה is beloved at its time? But it was taught: One who comes home on מוצאי שבת blesses over the wine, the light, and the spices, and then says הבדלה over the cup. If he has only one cup, he saves it until after the meal and says all of them together then. So we do not say a מצוה is beloved at its time!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back with a ברייתא about הבדלה. There, a person with one cup waits until after eating. This seems to show we don't insist on doing a מצוה right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one cup, the ברייתא says to save it for ברכת המזון after the meal, and to say הבדלה on it then. That means delaying הבדלה, even though its time came when שבת ended. If חביבה מצוה בשעתה were a real rule, הבדלה should be done immediately.

keyTerms.meaning: And do we really say?
The night after שבת ends
The blessing separating שבת from the weekday
He links them together in a chain (says them in a row)
The light (the fire/candle blessing)

steps.confusionAlert: 'מניחו עד לאחר המזון' does not mean he skips הבדלה. He still says it, just later, on the cup used for ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: And do we say that a מצוה is beloved at its time?
But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
One who enters his home on Saturday night
blesses over the wine,
and over the light, and over the spices,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ אוֹמֵר הַבְדָּלָה עַל הַכּוֹס.
phrases.english: and afterward says havdalah over the cup.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא כּוֹס אֶחָד —
phrases.english: And if he has only one cup —
he leaves it until after the meal
phrases.notes: He uses it for ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: and strings them all together after it,
phrases.notes: All the הבדלה blessings come right after ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: so we do not say that a מצוה is beloved at its time!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמְרִינַן חֲבִיבָה מִצְוָה בִּשְׁעָתָהּ? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle used in the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא allows delaying הבדלה until after the meal, which contradicts insisting on doing a מצוה at its time.

steps.title: He introduces his answer modestly
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says he is not a great thinker, only a teacher who passes on rulings, and the בית מדרש rules like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am not a wise man, nor a speculator, nor an outstanding individual. Rather, I am a teacher and arranger of teachings, and in the בית מדרש they rule like me.
steps.whatsHappening: Before giving his real answer, רב נחמן בר יצחק describes himself humbly. This step sets up the distinction he gives in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is saying: what follows is not my own clever invention. It is the accepted teaching, and it is the practice in the בית מדרש. This gives his distinction authority.

keyTerms.meaning: A wise man (a great scholar)
A seer or speculator (one who reasons on his own)
An outstanding individual
One who learns and arranges teachings (a transmitter of tradition)
The study hall

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא לָא חַכִּימָאָה אֲנָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: I am not a wise man,
nor am I a speculator,
nor am I an outstanding individual,
rather, I am a teacher and arranger of teachings,
and so they rule in the study hall, in accordance with me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the reply to the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Preface establishing the authority of the coming answer.

steps.title: Bringing שבת in versus taking it out
steps.stepSummary: We bring שבת in early to show love for it. We take שבת out late so it doesn't seem like a burden.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see a difference between bringing in the day and taking out the day. Bringing in the day: the earlier we do it, the better, and we show our love for it. Taking out the day: we delay it, so that it should not seem like a burden on us.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge. קידוש and הבדלה are different, so delaying הבדלה does not contradict doing קידוש right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying קידוש early shows we are eager for שבת. Rushing הבדלה would look like we can't wait for שבת to be over. So the rule of early קידוש does not carry over to הבדלה, and the ברייתא about הבדלה is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing in the day (the start of שבת)
Taking out the day (the end of שבת)
We show love for it
Like a burden or load

steps.whatToRemember: קידוש is done early to show love for שבת. הבדלה may be delayed so שבת doesn't look like a burden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This distinction explains why קידוש is not pushed off to the next day, while הבדלה may be pushed off until after the meal. Each one fits how we treat שבת: eager to bring it in, slow to see it go.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאנֵי לַן בֵּין עַיּוֹלֵי יוֹמָא לְאַפּוֹקֵי יוֹמָא:
phrases.english: For us there is a difference between bringing in the day and taking out the day:

phrases.aramaic: עַיּוֹלֵי יוֹמָא — כׇּל כַּמָּה דְּמַקְדְּמִינַן לֵיהּ עֲדִיף,
phrases.english: bringing in the day: the earlier we do it, the better,
and we show our love for it.
taking out the day: we delay it,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לֶיהֱוֵי עֲלַן כְּטוּנָא.
phrases.english: so that it should not be on us like a burden.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי לַן בֵּין עַיּוֹלֵי יוֹמָא לְאַפּוֹקֵי יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual content of the answer introduced in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Delaying הבדלה shows that חביבה מצוה בשעתה is not a real rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The start and end of שבת follow different logic, so both rulings stand.

steps.title: This ברייתא teaches eight lessons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that eight הלכות can be learned from the הבדלה ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this ברייתא eight things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the הבדלה ברייתא from step 4 and says it contains eight lessons. This line sets up a list that starts in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is finished. Now the גמרא mines the ברייתא for practical rules. Each following 'שמע מינה' will be one of the eight.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (a conclusion drawn from a source)
This ברייתא
Eight

phrases.english: Learn from this baraita eight things.
phrases.notes: That's the ברייתא about הבדלה quoted in step 4.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section: lessons drawn from the ברייתא of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eight הלכות can be derived from the הבדלה ברייתא.

steps.title: הבדלה in prayer still needs a cup
steps.stepSummary: Lesson one: even someone who said הבדלה in the תפלה must also say הבדלה over a cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it: one who said הבדלה in the תפלה must still say הבדלה over a cup.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first of the eight lessons. A person who already said הבדלה in מעריב must still make הבדלה over wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes someone coming home on מוצאי שבת, presumably after praying מעריב, where he said 'אתה חוננתנו'. Even so, he makes הבדלה on a cup at home. So the version in the תפלה does not replace the one on wine.

keyTerms.meaning: One who says הבדלה in the עמידה (אתה חוננתנו)
Over a cup (of wine)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of making הבדלה on wine at home even after saying אתה חוננתנו in מעריב.

phrases.english: Learn from it: one who says havdalah in the prayer —
must also say havdalah over the cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first item in the list of eight lessons announced in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הבדלה in the תפלה does not exempt a person from הבדלה over a cup.

steps.title: Lesson two: Grace after Meals needs a cup
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא we learn that ברכת המזון is said over a cup of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it: a blessing needs a cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second of the eight lessons. It learns that ברכת המזון needs a cup of wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ברכת המזון did not need a cup, the person would just make הבדלה right away with his one cup. Instead the ברייתא tells him to wait and save the cup for after the meal. That only makes sense if the cup is needed for ברכת המזון too.

keyTerms.meaning: And learn from it. This is the formula that pulls a rule out of a source.
A blessing. Here it means ברכת המזון, Grace after Meals.
Requires, needs
A cup of wine
Grace after Meals

steps.confusionAlert: The word בְּרָכָה here is not any blessing. It means ברכת המזון in particular, because that is the blessing the ברייתא's person saves the cup for.

phrases.english: And learn from it:
a blessing [of Grace after Meals] requires a cup.
phrases.notes: Otherwise he would make הבדלה now and not wait

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of eight lessons announced in step 7. This is lesson two, after lesson one in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ברכת המזון is said over a cup of wine. That is why the one cup is saved for after the meal.

steps.title: Lesson three: The cup of blessing needs a minimum amount
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא we learn that a כוס של ברכה must hold a set minimum amount of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it: a cup of blessing needs a minimum measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third lesson. A cup used for a ברכה must have at least a certain amount of wine in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why not split the one cup into two smaller cups, one for הבדלה now and one for ברכת המזון later? The ברייתא does not allow that. This shows that each cup needs a full minimum amount, so half a cup is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A cup of blessing: the cup of wine a ברכה is said over
Needs, requires
A set minimum amount (for this cup, a רְבִיעִית)
A quarter-לוג, the standard minimum for a כוס של ברכה

phrases.english: And learn from it:
a cup of blessing requires a minimum measure.
phrases.notes: Otherwise he could divide the one cup into two

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה צָרִיךְ שִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on lesson two. Since ברכת המזון needs a cup, we now ask why the one cup can't be split. The answer is that a cup needs a minimum amount.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A כוס של ברכה must have a minimum amount of wine, so one cup cannot be split in two.

steps.title: Lesson four: The one who blesses must taste
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא we learn that the person saying the ברכה over the cup must drink from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it: the one who says the blessing must taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the fourth lesson. Whoever says a ברכה over a cup must taste the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why not make הבדלה over the full cup without drinking it, and then use the same untouched cup for ברכת המזון? The ברייתא does not allow that. This shows that saying a ברכה over a cup requires drinking from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says the blessing
That he should taste, meaning drink from the cup
The blessing that separates שבת from the weekday

phrases.english: And learn from it:
one who recites a blessing must taste [from the cup].
phrases.notes: Otherwise he could make הבדלה without drinking and reuse the full cup

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off another way to use one cup twice. Lesson three ruled out splitting it, and now lesson four rules out leaving it untouched.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Saying a ברכה over a cup requires drinking from it.

steps.title: Lesson five: Tasting the cup spoils it for another blessing
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא we learn that once someone drinks from a cup, it is a 'damaged' cup and cannot be used for another ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it: tasting it damages it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the fifth lesson. A cup that was already drunk from is considered 'damaged' and is not fit for another ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why not make הבדלה, taste a little, and use what is left for ברכת המזון? The ברייתא does not allow that. This shows that drinking from the cup makes it unfit to be a כוס של ברכה again.

keyTerms.meaning: He tasted it
He damaged it (made it unfit)
A damaged cup: one that was already drunk from, so it can't be used for a ברכה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical rule that the wine left in a cup someone drank from is פָּגוּם. Such a cup must be fixed or refilled before it can be used for קידוש, הבדלה, or ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: And learn from it:
once he tasted it, he has damaged it.
phrases.notes: Otherwise he could taste for הבדלה and use the rest for ברכת המזון

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows directly from lesson four. The one who blesses must taste, and now we learn that tasting ruins the cup for a second ברכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Once a cup has been drunk from, it is פָּגוּם and can't serve as a כוס של ברכה.

steps.title: Lesson six: Even after eating, one still makes הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא we learn that someone who already ate after שבת without making הבדלה still makes הבדלה afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it: one who tasted [food] still makes הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the sixth lesson. Even if a person already ate before making הבדלה, he still makes הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the person eats his whole meal first and only makes הבדלה at the end over the saved cup. So eating before הבדלה does not cancel the מצוה. He still makes הבדלה afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: He tasted, meaning he ate food
Makes הבדלה
The night after שבת ends

steps.confusionAlert: Here טָעַם does NOT mean tasting the wine of the cup, as it did in the last two lessons. It means he ate food (his meal) before making הבדלה, and even so he still makes הבדלה.
steps.whatToRemember: So far the ברייתא of the one cup has taught six lessons. (1) הבדלה in תפלה still needs a cup. (2) ברכת המזון needs a cup. (3) The cup needs a minimum amount. (4) The one who blesses must drink. (5) Drinking makes the cup פָּגוּם. (6) Eating first does not cancel הבדלה.

phrases.english: And learn from it:
one who has tasted [food] still recites הבדלה.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא's person ate his meal and only then made הבדלה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from lessons about the cup itself to a lesson about timing. Eating before הבדלה does not cancel it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A person who ate before making הבדלה still makes הבדלה afterward.
